headline_marked: Meta Muse AI [[offers to set up SSH]] to private VMs, raising security concerns
headline: Meta Muse AI offers to set up SSH to private VMs, raising security concerns
summary: The AI agent, running on AMD EPYC servers, has reportedly offered to establish SSH connections to user VMs, potentially creating security loopholes.
details: Meta's AI agent, Muse, is reportedly running on AMD EPYC 9D25 host systems, with each user sandbox allocated two CPU cores and 8GB of memory. Researchers have discovered that Muse can execute basic Ubuntu commands and has even offered to set up SSH connections to private virtual machines.

This capability has raised security concerns, as a malicious actor could potentially leverage a reverse SSH tunnel to bypass firewalls and execute more damaging commands. While Muse currently has permission limitations, the offer to set up SSH is a notable vulnerability.

Muse has surpassed 500,000 daily active users, highlighting the massive scale of its operation. To support this user base, Meta is estimated to be using around 2,000 server trays, each equipped with dual EPYC 9D25 CPUs and 2TB of memory, underscoring the significant hardware investment.

The AI agent isolates itself to CPU-only sandboxes, with Meta utilizing separate GPU servers for inference tasks. This CPU-centric approach is likely chosen due to the high core density of AMD's EPYC processors, which allows for efficient hosting of a large number of users.

Muse is currently available on Android, iOS, and MacOS, with browser access also provided for users with a Meta account. The potential security implications of its command execution capabilities are a growing concern as the platform expands.

headline_marked: SpaceX Starship [[completes orbital flight rehearsal]] ahead of Sept. 28 launch
headline: SpaceX Starship completes orbital flight rehearsal ahead of Sept. 28 launch
summary: The rocket successfully ran through a full launch simulation, including propellant loading and countdown, paving the way for its first orbital test flight.
details: SpaceX has successfully completed a wet dress rehearsal for its Starship rocket, a critical step before its 14th test flight. This rehearsal simulated the entire launch sequence, including loading propellants and running through the countdown, ensuring all systems are go for the upcoming mission.

The Starship Flight 14 is scheduled for September 28, with a 75-minute launch window opening at 8:15 AM ET. This flight marks a significant milestone as it will be Starship's first attempt at an orbital trajectory after multiple suborbital tests.

During the orbital flight, Starship is planned to circle Earth six times over 10 hours before re-entering the atmosphere and splashing down in the ocean. The mission will also deploy 26 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites into orbit, expanding SpaceX's satellite internet constellation.

The successful rehearsal indicates that SpaceX is on track for the launch. The company announced the completion of the rehearsal on X, formerly Twitter, sharing that the vehicle is now ready for its next major test.
